subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should own OpenClaw's public domain egress control: a scoped web_fetch allow/deny policy, a cross-tool web policy covering fetch/search/browser/provider fallback/cache/redirects, or the managed-proxy boundary?
rationale: This becomes an operator-trusted outbound security boundary and the open related PRs implement incompatible answers that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Contract
options.body: Define the cross-tool policy first so web_fetch, search, browser, redirects, cache, provider fallback, and proxy behavior do not ship conflicting guarantees.

options.title: Accept Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Land a narrow web_fetch hostname/domain policy as an interim contract and keep deny domains, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy Boundary
options.body: Make proxy.enabled plus operator-managed proxy policy the owner for app egress and avoid adding local domain-firewall config to web tools.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Egress Contract
recommendation.body: Define the cross-tool policy first so web_fetch, search, browser, redirects, cache, provider fallback, and proxy behavior do not ship conflicting guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across SSRF helpers, guarded fetch, web_fetch runtime/docs, and adjacent OpenAI/Codex provider routing.
